target_customer: Restaurants sending just in time promotions to customers
problem: Restaurants had empty tables and unsold capacity at predictable times and needed a way to promote on short notice.
business_model: Restaurant promotion platform, pricing not found

competitors.name: Groupon
competitors.what: Daily deal service, restaurants a major category, 17 more cities by October 2009
competitors.traction_then: Expanded from Chicago late 2008 to 17 more cities by Oct 2009

technical_complexity.rationale: Web promotion and messaging tools for small merchants.

defensibility.rationale: No data or network advantage is documented; promotion tools were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Groupon and OpenTable launched restaurant deals in 2010 per Bloomberg coverage; no source ties this to InstantQ.

market_need_then: Restaurants were adopting deal sites in 2009 (Groupon growth); no direct evidence of InstantQ customers found.

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the brand beyond the name and a short YC profile, so no evidence of brand pull was found.

outcome_analysis: InstantQ was a two person Summer 2009 company offering restaurant promotions and is listed inactive. No funding, traction, shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause of its end is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. A low quality database describes it as a retail queue management product, which conflicts with YC and may be a different company or an error; not used. Founder backgrounds not found.
